brand_note: Fictional brand made up for this demo. Gus, the narrator and the offer are fictional too. The brand name is typeset by the edit step; no storyboard still carries it.

A.label: Named underdog

fragments.text: This sad, droopy little fig is Gus.

A.kept: A named underdog in the first breath, shown at his lowest.
A.changed: A rescue puppy becomes Gus, a fiddle-leaf fig; the line is ours.
A.call: A name makes people care before they know what is being sold. Same device as the source, so this is the control the other two openings are tested against.

B.label: Confession

fragments.text: I almost put Gus out on the curb.

B.kept: The underdog named in the first line, at his lowest.
B.changed: Told as a confession: she nearly put him out on the curb.
B.call: A confession makes the viewer ask what changed her mind, and the body answers it.

C.label: Reversal

fragments.text: Gus wasn't thirsty. He was drowning.

C.kept: The underdog named in the first line, at his lowest.
C.changed: Opens on a reversal: the problem was too much water, not too little.
C.call: It corrects what most owners assume, so the viewer stays for the reason.

beats.name: Arrival

fragments.text: He moved in with me two springs ago.

beats.call: One line of shared history raises the stakes without slowing the opening. It sits on the widest shot of the film, so the room reads before the close-ups.

beats.name: What it costs

fragments.text: I adore him, but: brown spots,
leaves on the floor every morning,
and a water ring on my landlord's rug.

beats.call: Specific damage is believable; 'struggling' on its own is not. One cut per spoken item, on its first word: the cut follows the voice, not a clock.

beats.name: Tried it all

fragments.text: I knew it wasn't his fault.

beats.call: Clearing Gus moves the blame to the old routine, and each failed fix answers 'why not just do X' before the viewer asks. A cut on each fix, then the longest pause of the body after the line of defeat.

beats.name: The find

fragments.text: It waters him from below, and the little dial tells me when he's thirsty.
Now he's putting out new leaves.

beats.call: The product enters as the turn of the story: a plain box at the door, its name typeset on screen by the edit step. One mechanism line, shown on the dial. No health claim: a fictional brand has no results to quote, so the change is a new leaf.

beats.name: The ask

fragments.text: If your plant's been struggling, try it.
Link below. First planter ships free.

beats.call: The ask names the viewer's own situation, over the recovered plant. Then the name card, and Gus's name signs off, so the opening pays off.
